results.evidence: Still only one source gives a commitment numeral for Frenzel Spitz: the 2004 AAJ Southern Picket Enchainment account calls it "II 5.6", which supports the commitment chip, not the three row fields that say Grade III. The 1962 AAJ first-ascent article gives no grade for Frenzelspitz, and the Alpinist, mountainwerks 2004 and Lemke traverse accounts do not grade it either; rhinoclimbs' peak history is now a 404. A second independent source giving II (or III) would settle it.

The only sourced rappel is still the one off the north side of the Otto-Himmel col (Holsten 2011, which used a pin, a slung block and a nut). No source for summit-gully rappels, a 70 m single-rappel option or a 'Crossover Descent' turned up: AAJ 2004 gives no descent details, and the Lemke, mountainwerks and Alpinist traverse accounts do not describe a descent from Frenzel Spitz. The RAPPELS text stays unconfirmed. A trip report that describes the descent off Frenzel Spitz's summit would settle it.

Sources still disagree about the rating. One party calls it 'Serious Class 3', says it is loose terrain where you must not slip, and puts the crest near 6,400 ft. Another description has you cross a moat onto low-fifth-class ground. A third calls it harrowing scrambling up loose ledges. No two independent sources agree on one rating. Consensus from a guidebook-grade source (for example Beckey) would settle it.

Parties camp at different heights. One camped at about 6,400 ft on the Chopping Block ridge above Crescent Creek Basin; others report the ~5,800 ft band, or about 6,050 ft below Mount Terror. A USGS point reading at the stored camp pin gives about 4,190 ft, so the pin itself is misplaced (pin positions are out of scope) and cannot adjudicate. No single camp elevation is supported by two sources. Settling it would take agreement on one named camp spot, plus a coordinate for it.

SR-20 to Newhalem is open in winter, and the Goodell Creek Campground runs year-round. But the Upper Goodell group-camp spur, where the old roadbed starts, is described only as a steep, narrow dirt road. Its access improves as snow melts, and a 2020 report mentions a gate with a landslide-closure sign. Whether that spur is closed in winter is unconfirmed, and the NPS and recreation.gov pages for the group camp do not show season dates. The park stating the spur's winter status would settle it.

The 2020 trip report puts the route a 5-minute walk from the car. The area page has the unmarked trail climbing the boulder field from the pullout, with the Mossness wall visible through the trees above it. The route page gives only '6+ hours' for the ascent and descent and states no approach time, distance or total gain. USGS point readings put the pullout at about 3,180 ft, the start of Bad-Tempered Prom Queen (the first pitch) at about 3,340 ft, and the Full Montey topout at about 4,880 ft (the area page says 4,916 ft), roughly 0.6 mi straight-line from the car. That strongly suggests the stored 2,700 ft gain and the 2.5 mi topout distance are too high, but no outside source states a replacement gain or distance, and changing the 0.75 h approach alone would break timing.totalHrs = 6. A published car-to-car gain figure or approach time would settle it.

results.fact: North Fork Wolf Creek crossing distance
results.evidence: Still split. One source puts the crossing (a fire-damaged log bridge) at 2.6 miles, and an older description puts the ford at 2.3 miles. A third report captions a bridge at about 2 miles on the Wolf Creek trail without naming the creek. The Forest Service, Willhite, trailcatjim, hikingproject and go-washington pages give no mileage for the crossing. A measured GPS track, or a second source for either figure, would settle it.

results.fact: Line of the 40-50 degree traverse (under the West Peak vs across the East Peak's SW face)
results.evidence: The 2004 report places the 40-50 degree slopes on the East Peak's southwest face, after a 400 ft climb of its west ridge from the saddle. A 2025 report likewise hugs the steep west ridge of the East Peak and bypasses outcrops on the south slope. The 'traverse below the West Peak on its south side' line is also described (search summary of the route-and-place page, which blocked a direct fetch) but with no slope angle. So the steep ground seems to be on the East Peak, and the variant may simply misplace the angle. However, no source states the angle of the sidehill under the West Peak, and correcting it means rewriting the variant's baseFinding prose. A description giving slope angles for the West Peak sidehill would settle it.
